title: Strata of a flat constructible sheaf and generation by $a_!L$
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $X$ a Noetherian scheme (for
instance of finite type over the standing field), on the étale or the
pro-étale site.

1. If $F$ is a flat constructible sheaf of $A$-modules on $X$, there is a
finite partition $X=\bigsqcup_{k=1}^mS_k$ into locally closed subschemes,
ordered so that $X_{\ge k}=\bigcup_{k'\ge k}S_{k'}$ is closed and $S_k$ is open in
$X_{\ge k}$, such that each $F|_{S_k}$ is locally constant with stalks finite
projective $A$-modules.
2. For such a partition, with $a_k:S_k\hookrightarrow X$ the inclusions and
$L_k=F|_{S_k}$, $F$ is an iterated extension of the sheaves $a_{k!}L_k$; each
$a_{k!}L_k$ is flat constructible and lies in $\Dctf(X,A)$.
3. $\Dctf(X,A)$ is the smallest full subcategory of $D(X,A)$ containing the
objects $a_!L$ ($a:S\hookrightarrow X$ locally closed, $L$ locally constant
with finite projective stalks) and closed under shifts, extensions (cones)
and direct summands.

Conventions. On either small site use ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring $A$ and their unbounded derived category. Here $\Dctf$ consists of objects with bounded constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in some finite interval: $H^r(C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}N[0])=0$ outside the interval for every module sheaf $N$. Flat means that ordinary tensoring with the sheaf is exact; finite projective means a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module. For a locally closed immersion $a$, factor it as the open immersion $j$ into its scheme-theoretic closure followed by the closed immersion $g$ into $X$ and write $a_!=g_*j_!$. The subcategories in clause (3) are understood to be closed under isomorphisms. A partition of the empty scheme may have no strata.

proof.text: Work over a finite commutative ring and a Noetherian scheme. The existing Noetherian-space and immersion instances make the scheme-theoretic-image factorization quasi-compact where required. All canonical extension functors and all theorem signatures are retained, including arbitrary nonreduced stratum domains and the empty scheme.

For the etale ordered stratification, use the existing constructible-sheaf comparison, choose an adapted stratification, and apply the source Devissage.exists_chain_opens construction. Successive differences refine the original strata, and their tails are the complements of the preceding opens. Finite local constancy pulls back along the refinement. Flat pullback and flat geometric fibers, followed by finitePresentation_of_finite and Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation, give finite projective stalks.

For intrinsic pro-etale coefficients, restrict scalars to ULift(A). The canonical realization counit identifies the realized restricted sheaf with the original one. The proved intrinsic_flat_iff transports flatness; coefficient_constructible_iff transports constructibility. The fixed-module constructible-origin theorem supplies a constructible etale origin. Apply the same ordered open-chain refinement to that origin, then use the pullback comparison and finiteLocal_iff to obtain finite locally constant intrinsic restrictions. The geometric point of ProEtaleFiniteModelStalks preserves flatness. A module-colimit cocone whose scalar equation is coefficientGerm_smul identifies the fixed and intrinsic coefficient stalks. Thus each finite stalk is flat and finitely presented over the finite ring, hence projective. No conservativity of pro-etale geometric stalks is invoked.

For an ordered etale partition, put U_r equal to the complement of the tail starting at r, including U_0 empty and U_n=X. The tower M_r=(U_r)! (F restricted to U_r) starts at zero and ends at F. Inside U_(r+1), the given stratum S_r is a closed subscheme complementary to U_r. Apply the open-closed short exact sequence and then exact open extension to X. The counit-composition isomorphism identifies the first term with M_r. The canonical locally closed extension comparison identifies the quotient with a_(r)! (F restricted to S_r). Transport the sequence with ShortComplex.isoMk. This uses the actual stratum schemes without replacing them by reduced subschemes.

For the pro-etale filtration, choose the constructible etale origin of the restricted coefficient sheaf. Flatness of that origin follows by reflecting finite limits through the fully faithful strong monoidal comparison functor. Map its etale filtration through exact comparison followed by intrinsic realization. The proved source ordinary quasi-compact quasi-separated direct-image comparison, the canonical open-extension comparison, and the intrinsic pullback encoding identify each mapped quotient with exactly the canonical pro-etale locally closed extension in the theorem. A private general exact-functor filtration lemma transports the endpoint and all quotient isomorphisms. The etale extension of each restricted origin is flat and constructible, so its intrinsic comparison, and therefore the specified quotient, is flat constructible too.

For every intrinsic lisse sheaf with finite projective stalks, the fixed-module lisse-origin theorem gives a finite locally constant etale origin. The canonical comparison on geometric stalks and the intrinsic/fixed stalk isomorphism identify its algebraically closed geometric fibers with the projective intrinsic stalks. The conservative family of algebraic-closure points on the etale site detects flatness of the etale origin. Its canonical locally closed extension is flat constructible by the existing etale open-closed flatness and constructibility APIs. The extension comparison transports this to the intrinsic generator. A flat intrinsic sheaf placed in degree zero has bounded constructible cohomology: degree-zero homology is the sheaf and all other homology vanishes. The fixed-scalar flat-single theorem and intrinsic Tor transport give Tor interval [0,0]. This proves the generator properties as well as the remaining assertions of clause (2).

source.place: Clauses (2) and (3), all locally closed generators

proof.text: The intrinsic constructible coefficient class contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, kernels, cokernels and extensions by constructibleCoefficient_exactClosure. Its derived homology property, intersected with boundedness, is triangulated by the general weak-Serre-class theorem. Finite Tor amplitude is triangulated: use the proved tensor_functor and tensor_homology_vanishes helpers for the full intrinsic K-flat tensor test. Tensoring preserves zero, shifts move [a,b] to [a-m,b-m], and the homology exact sequence gives middle-term vanishing after widening endpoint intervals. For retracts, each constructible sheaf retract is the kernel of the complementary idempotent; cohomological bounds pass through homology retracts; tensor homology retracts preserve the Tor interval. Hence the expanded intrinsic Dctf property is thick.

The etale thick-generation theorem already proved in this module uses its specified filtration, the independent bounded flat constructible model, and induction on a strictly bounded complex via HomotopyCategory.mem_subcategory_of_strictly_bounded. For intrinsic generation, transfer this proved etale result. Realization is an exact equivalence; reflect the intrinsic bounded constructible cohomology and Tor interval to a fixed-module derived object. boundedConstructible_of_homology and the fixed-module sheaf origin theorem supply a bounded constructible etale origin. The source comparison Tor-interval theorem gives that origin finite Tor amplitude. The inverse image of the intrinsic generator envelope under derived comparison-realization is thick and contains every etale generator: finite locally constant flat etale sheaves realize to intrinsic lisse sheaves with finite projective stalks, and single objects commute with exact derived functors and the canonical extension comparison. The etale generation theorem therefore puts the original intrinsic object in that envelope. Conversely every intrinsic generator belongs to intrinsic Dctf by the previous generator calculation, and thickness gives the whole envelope.

The item statement is the blueprint's with the accepted Conventions; nothing is weakened and the coefficients are ordinary constant-A modules on both sites. L1 (open/closed flatness) is true: j^*, i^* are exact, commute with tensor and are jointly conservative, and its pro-etale direction uses exactness of i_* under the quasi-compact j that the node assumes. L2 holds because a surjective closed immersion is integral, universally injective and surjective, so 09AB/04DZ give topos equivalences with h^{-1}A=A, and finite (projective) local models are reflected by refining covers through the equivalence. L3 clause 1 is 0GJ1 with a closed immersion; clauses 2-3 follow because the scheme-theoretic closure commutes with restriction to an open for quasi-compact immersions over Noetherian X. Tested on empty U/Z, Spec k -> Spec k[eps], S empty and nonreduced S. None is a duplicate: lemma-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-extension-zero covers only L3 clause 1, and the topological-invariance nodes are set-valued or condensed. None restates an item clause. Each step's citations say what is used: cell refinement and ordering, stalk projectivity via the topos point, nonreduced first stratum via the L2 unit and L3 or the pro-etale coherence node (its factorization-independence and gamma composition paragraphs checked), D_k closed surjective base change, thickness via the constructible and Tor comparisons (qcqs X, Noetherian A checked), lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible for a general finite ring and Noetherian X, and brutal truncations. proof_deps equals the union of uses, the closure of 1965 nodes has no cycle and no missing or merged ids, and no SGA source is used. lean.note: All three clauses are stated separately for both sites. The six helper definitions are constituents of this node: ordered tails, its finite extension filtration, lisse finite-projective stalk conditions, and canonical locally closed extensions through the scheme-theoretic image. Dctf is expanded as bounded constructible cohomology and the recorded finite Tor-amplitude condition, as the node conventions specify. Four already-landed statement dependencies are added for the coefficient-linear stalk, retained local-constancy construction, intrinsic realization, and inverse image. No other DAG node is stated. Rework restoration (A4, 2026-10-21): restore the complete quarantined module, including the three existing etale proofs and three original pro-etale holes. Replace the retired Scheme.LocallyClosedStratification by Scheme.Stratification in the ordered predicate and the ordered-stratification/filtration statements. On the Noetherian schemes in this node, constructibility of locally closed strata is automatic; the mathematical statement and every dependency are preserved.
